ID-2026-S1438.aiSummary: The law cuts $13.5 million from the Idaho Digital Learning Academy for fiscal year 2027 and reduces the related transfer from the state general fund by the same amount. It also bars withdrawals from the Public Education Stabilization Fund for the academy during that year and says the academy must use existing cash and may reduce offerings or turn away eligible enrollments to keep a positive cash balance. The academy must also submit reports on course compliance with state rules on diversity, equity, inclusion, and on its funding and course costs. It became law and takes effect on July 1, 2026.

ID-2026-S1430.aiSummary: This law tightens Idaho’s rules on local firearm laws. It says counties, cities, and other local bodies generally cannot make or enforce their own rules on firearm sale, ownership, carrying, storage, and related items, and it sets a $10,000 civil penalty for willful violations. It also lets the attorney general, or a person or group harmed by a bad local rule, seek damages, court orders, or other relief after giving notice and time to fix the problem. It took effect on April 2, 2026.

It would make it unlawful for those employers to knowingly hire or refer a worker whose work status has not been checked, and it sets steps for state enforcement and court penalties. The law would take effect on January 1, 2027.

ID-2026-H896.aiSummary: The bill would set up a process for the attorney general to handle claims that a public officer, public employee, or public agency broke certain Idaho laws. It would require notice and a chance to fix the issue first, then allow a court order to make them comply if needed. In some cases, it would also allow removal from public office or public employment for up to five years and let the winning side recover attorney fees.
